ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the triangular paper $ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $\angle A=30^\circ$, and $AC=9$. Fold the paper so that point $C$ falls on point $D$ on side $AB$, and the fold line $BE$ intersects $AC$ at point $E$. What is the length of the fold line $BE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle C=90^\circ$ and $\angle A=30^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle ABC=60^\circ$.\\
Since the paper is folded such that point C lies on point D on side AB,\\
it follows that $\angle CBE=\angle ABE=30^\circ$, CE=DE, and $\angle ADE=90^\circ$,\\
which implies that $\angle A=\angle ABE$ and AE=2CE\\
Therefore, AE=BE=\boxed{6}.

it follows that $\angle ABC=60^\circ$.\\
Since the paper is folded such that point C lies on point D on side AB,\\
it follows that $\angle CBE=\angle ABE=30^\circ$, CE=DE, and $\angle ADE=90^\circ$,\\
which implies that $\angle A=\angle ABE$ and AE=2CE\\
Therefore, AE=BE=\boxed{6}.
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the triangular paper $ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $\angle A=30^\circ$, and $AC=9$. Fold the paper so that point $C$ falls on point $D$ on side $AB$, and the fold line $BE$ intersects $AC$ at point $E$. What is the length of the fold line $BE$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle C=90^\circ$ and $\angle A=30^\circ$,\\ it follows that $\angle ABC=60^\circ$.\\ Since the paper is folded such that point C lies on point D on side AB,\\ it follows that $\angle CBE=\angle ABE=30^\circ$, CE=DE, and $\angle ADE=90^\circ$,\\ which implies that $\angle A=\angle ABE$ and AE=2CE\\ Therefore, AE=BE=\boxed{6}.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is triangle ABC, C is at the lower left and marked with a right angle, A is at the lower right, B is at the upper left; AC is the base, AB is the hypotenuse. Point D is on side AB, point E is on side AC, segment BE is drawn as a crease, indicating folding C to D on AB. Then reason: Given ∠C=90°, ∠A=30°, so ∠ABC=60°. When folding, C lands on D, and B remains fixed on the crease BE, therefore ray BC is reflected to ray BD; also D is on AB, so BD is in the same direction as BA, hence BE bisects ∠CBA. Therefore ∠CBE=∠EBA=30°. In right triangle BCE, ∠C=90° and ∠CBE=30°; according to the 30-60-90 triangle ratio, CE is half of the hypotenuse BE, that is CE=BE/2. In triangle ABE, ∠A=30°, ∠ABE=30°, so the sides opposite them are equal, AE=BE. Also AC=AE+CE=9, so BE+BE/2=9, giving 3BE/2=9, BE=6.
